title: 1609년 강원도의 하늘

images.prompt: A Joseon-era Korean hanok courtyard on a clear sunny afternoon, 1609: under the tiled eaves, just above the packed dirt ground, a round glowing disc of soft light about the size of a washbasin is slowly rising into the air. Paper sliding doors, a clay storage jar, wooden veranda. Quiet and eerie.

Wide view of a small Joseon-era village on the Korean east coast near Yangyang, 1609: tiled and thatched roofs, pine-covered mountains behind, the sea in the distance, a perfectly clear cloudless blue afternoon sky.

In a clear blue sky above Joseon hanok roofs, a floating glowing orb of light that is white on its left side, blue in the middle and red on its right side, splitting into two pieces: one piece dispersing like drifting smoke, the other hovering flat like a cushion.

A Joseon-era hanok courtyard: three villagers in white hanbok seen from far behind as small faceless silhouettes, standing still and looking up at an empty perfectly clear sky, startled, as if hearing distant thunder.
Early morning over a Joseon-era coastal town by the sea (Gangneung), 1609: a red glowing light shaped like a bottle gourd falling slowly from a clear sky toward the rooftops, calm sea and pine trees.
A wide river valley with rice fields and a small Joseon-era town (Wonju), clear sky: a long red glowing ribbon of light like a strip of red cloth flowing across the sky from one side to the other.
A Joseon-era riverside town (Chuncheon) under a clear sky: a big fireball the size of a large earthenware jar streaking low across the sky like a flying arrow, leaving a bright trail over the river.
Pine-covered hills by the east sea near a small Joseon-era town (Ganseong), morning: a pale ring of smoke shaped like a sun halo hanging in the clear sky, quiet and strange.

Close view of an old hand-painted Korean map of Gangwon province on aged hanji paper on a low wooden desk, mountains and rivers drawn in ink, five small red seal marks scattered on it; all writing is blurred and unreadable. A single warm candle light.
Bright daytime sky over Korean mountains: a huge fireball meteor streaking across the sky, breaking apart into two glowing pieces, leaving a long white smoke trail that lingers in the clear sky.

Boogi the owl archivist sits at an old wooden desk in a dark archive room at night, holding a small amber lantern over an open old Korean bound book with yellowed pages (writing blurred and unreadable), shelves of old books behind fading into darkness. The owl looks thoughtfully at the viewer.
